tasks.short: Check applications and decide licence qualification.

steps.what: Evaluate completeness and accuracy of applications.
Determine whether applicants are qualified for licenses.
Record the qualification decision and the reason.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} form checks whether the application is complete and whether the typed facts match the attached documents. The registry clerk determines whether the applicant is qualified for the licence and records the reason. A failed completeness check returns the form. It is not a refusal. The screen never refuses a licence on its own.
tasks.previous_blocker: Completeness and qualification were one conversation, so a missing page and a real refusal looked the same.
tasks.enabler_now: Required fields and document matches can be checked as rules. Qualification is still a legal decision.
tasks.still_hard: Some licence rules need a fact that is not on the form, and national rules differ by permit type.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk can explain a refusal, and can see a match that is true but looks wrong on the page.

ambition.what: Return an incomplete application in the same week to people who now wait because nobody noticed a missing page.

tasks.altitude: Incomplete forms come back quickly. The clerk still decides qualification, and still signs the reason. The screen gains no refusal right.

reach.task: Decide whether an applicant meets a benefit rule, and record the reason.
reach.learn: That decision stays with the interviewer. This clerk does the same for a licence, and does not automate the refusal.

evidence.claim: Required fields and a document match can be checked without deciding the licence. The decision itself is a separate step.

The job digest says GDPR article 22 bars a solely automated decision with legal effect unless a legal ground applies, and that a score someone relies on can be the decision. Dutch UAVG article 40, as the digest states it, allows automation for a public task but not profiling. This desk does not refuse a licence by machine. Benefit-eligibility rules are a different decision and are not applied here.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Application id, required field names, and attached document ids, produced by the applicant and the form. Qualification reason is written by the clerk, not by the completeness result. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing application screen's required fields before a new rules engine.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the clerk.
A completeness failure is sent back as an incomplete form. It is not stored as a refusal.
unknowns: Which permit types this municipality issues.
Who else may sign a refusal.
research_questions: What share of applications fail only for a missing field?
Which qualification rules are written as fields?

already_counted.description: The clerk still records the decision and the reason.

incremental.description: The clerk updates a required field when a permit rule changes.

approvals.approved_version: application id and the decision text and reason shown to the clerk

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Qualification stays with the clerk, so the saving is the completeness check only. It shrinks when most applications fail for a reason that is not a missing field.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Prepare ordinances from the adopted decision.

loop.input: the adopted decision fields and the instrument template
loop.output: an ordinance, resolution, or proclamation draft
loop.check: each clause cites a decision field
loop.stop: stop when a decision field is empty
loop.why_not_simpler: the legal sentences are not a single mail-merge cell

steps.what: Check resolutions before they are executed.
Archive the signed proclamations for distribution.

tasks.design: A draft ordinance, resolution, or proclamation is prepared in {DOCS} only from the decision the council already adopted. The registry clerk checks it before anyone executes it. After signature, the text is archived for distribution. The draft does not adopt the decision. An empty decision field stops the draft.
tasks.previous_blocker: The clerk retyped last year's instrument and hoped the new decision matched the old clauses.
tasks.enabler_now: An adopted decision with fields can fill clauses. Execution still needs a check and a signature.
tasks.still_hard: A decision taken orally in the meeting has no fields until the minute exists.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk sees a clause that cites the wrong article or softens a vote.
tasks.altitude: Retyping a clear decision shrinks. The clerk still checks the text before it can be executed, recorded, or sent out.

reach.task: Prepare a document from notes someone else has already approved.
reach.learn: The approval stays upstream. This clerk still checks the instrument before it is executed.

evidence.claim: Clauses that cite decision fields can be assembled. A missing field cannot be filled with a likely sentence.

Executing an ordinance is a legal act. The clerk checks the text. The screen does not execute it. The job digest's justice high-risk point is about deciding cases, not about archiving a council text the council already adopted.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Decision id, instrument type, and clause fields, produced by the signed council minute. Empty clause fields stop the draft. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing instrument templates in {DOCS} before writing new ones.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the clerk.
unknowns: Whether distribution is on paper, post, or the municipal page.
research_questions: Are council decisions already fields when the clerk starts?
Which instrument types share one template?

already_counted.description: The clerk still checks the text before execution.

incremental.description: The clerk updates a template when the council changes a standard clause.

approvals.approved_version: decision id and the draft text shown to the clerk
checked text id about to be archived

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If decisions are not written as fields, the clerk drafts from the minute by hand and the saving stays near the low end. Fielded decisions keep the high end.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Issue municipal permits and collect fees.

steps.what: Calculate the fee for the permit type.
Issue marriage, dog, or other municipal licenses.
Collect the appropriate fees and write a receipt.

tasks.design: The {ERP} tariff calculates the fee for a permit type this municipality issues. The registry clerk issues the marriage, dog, or other municipal licence, and collects the fee and writes the receipt. Fishing or hunting permits are issued here only where this municipality actually issues them. The fee quote does not issue the licence. A type that is not on the tariff stops the quote.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fees were looked up in a paper table, and the licence and the receipt were two hand-written acts that could disagree.
tasks.enabler_now: A tariff with a permit type can quote a fee. Issuing the licence is still the clerk at the counter.
tasks.still_hard: Identity, impediments to marriage, and local permit rules are not a price.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk sees the person, the document, and whether this counter is allowed to issue that permit at all.
tasks.altitude: The fee is no longer a hunt through a table. The clerk still issues the licence and still takes the money. The screen issues nothing.

reach.task: Take the amount the tariff states and write a receipt.
reach.learn: The receipt is not the licence. This clerk still decides to issue.

evidence.claim: A tariff table can quote a fee for a known permit type. It cannot issue the permit.

Issuing a licence changes a person's legal position. The job digest says that kind of decision is not taken by a machine alone. The clerk issues it. Marriage and dog licences follow national rules. This is not a consumer-credit decision.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Permit type and tariff id, produced by the tariff table. The application must already carry the clerk's qualification decision from the earlier task. A missing decision stops issuance. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing tariff in {ERP} before a new fee app.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the clerk.
Hunting and fishing permits are out of scope unless this municipality issues them.
unknowns: Which permits this counter may issue.
Whether the fee is taken before or after issuance.
research_questions: Which permit types are on the tariff?
Who may issue a marriage record?

already_counted.description: The clerk still issues the licence.
The clerk still collects the fee and writes the receipt.

incremental.description: The clerk updates a tariff row when the fee changes.

approvals.approved_version: application id, permit type, and fee quote shown to the clerk

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Issuing and taking money stay at the counter, so the saving is the fee lookup. It shrinks when many requests are for permits this municipality does not issue.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Issue public notice of official meetings.

steps.what: Draft public notification of official meetings.

loop.input: the meeting record fields and the notice template
loop.check: date, place, and body match the meeting record
loop.stop: stop when date or place is empty
loop.why_not_simpler: the notice wording is local, not one fixed sentence

steps.what: Check the notice against the official agenda.
Issue the approved notification on the municipal page.

tasks.design: A public notification is drafted from the meeting record in {CALENDAR}: date, place, and the official body. The registry clerk checks it against the agenda. Only then does {CMS} publish it. The draft does not invent an activity. A meeting with no place is not published.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notices were retyped from the agenda, and a wrong room was spotted by the public.
tasks.enabler_now: A meeting record with date and place can fill a notice. Publishing still needs the clerk's check.
tasks.still_hard: A meeting can change after the notice, and some activities must not be public.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk knows which item is closed and must not appear in the public notice.

ambition.what: Publish a notice for a small committee meeting the same day it is fixed, not only for the council meeting.

tasks.altitude: Retyping the date and place shrinks. The clerk still decides the notice is fit to publish, including what to leave out.

reach.role: Hotel, Motel, and Resort Desk Clerks
reach.task: Post the hours and the place a guest can rely on.
reach.learn: A published time must match the record. This clerk still removes a closed item.

evidence.claim: Date, place, and body can fill a notice template. A closed agenda item must be left out by a person.
Publishing an official notice is an external act. The clerk checks it first. The job digest does not treat a meeting notice as a justice decision.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Meeting id, date, place, and body, produced by the meeting record. Agenda items carry a public or closed flag set by the clerk's office. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing meeting record and municipal page before a new site.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the clerk.
unknowns: Which meetings must be notified, and how many days ahead.
Who may publish besides this clerk.
research_questions: Are date and place always on the meeting record?

already_counted.description: The clerk still checks the notice against the agenda.

incremental.description: The clerk updates the notice template when the required wording changes.

approvals.approved_version: meeting id and the notice text shown to the clerk
checked notice id about to be published

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If date or place is often empty, the clerk writes the notice and the saving stays near the low end. Complete meeting records keep the high end.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The clerk still decides who qualifies, still issues the permit, and still checks a resolution. Completeness checks, fee sums, and notice drafts leave the hour.
reach: Eligibility interviewers decide a benefit themselves, and this desk learns not to copy that decision into a licence refusal.
Tellers take a fee only for the amount the tariff states, and this desk learns the receipt is not the permit.
skills_to_grow: Separate a missing field from a decision that the applicant does not qualify.
Issue only a permit type this municipality actually issues, and say so when it does not.
role.ambitious_version: A complete dog-licence application is ready for the clerk the same week, and the qualification decision still waits for the clerk.
